forks.decision: External tasks run fully native with a local checkout without upstream history, a local uv venv or Go/Rust toolchain, and our replay of the instance's FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS tests; no Docker
One evolutionary loop mutates code and text; a candidate is a commit
The loop engine is GEPA optimize_anything with repeat runs on frontier candidates
The loop may mutate only src and prompts; winners land as human-reviewed draft PRs
The judge labels per-task applicability and critiques each rollout for reflection only; grader correctness is the only objective
The Phase 4 power gate is retired; every paid run requires an explicit spend ceiling

contradictions: Approach cross-curd invariant 2 ('No optimizer-side model reads grader inputs') and the F-5 rationale in Decisions (proposer isolation 'keeps grader inputs out of the proposer's view, so the loop cannot steer the score through ... leaked tests') conflict with AC-2 and the interface sketch. AC-2 requires every reflective record to be built 'from the stored JSONL row', and evolve.propose_src_patch(worktree, records) passes those records to the proposer. Every stored row carries the grader's verdict text in `correctness_reason` (benchmark/run.py:851). For required-string tasks that text names the missing ground-truth string ('Missing: {required}', benchmark/tasks/base.py:178-180). For gin_edit_render_context it holds the last 1200 characters of held-out test output ('Trusted tests failed: ...', benchmark/tasks/gin_render_context_tasks.py:152-153). External tasks add grade_details with F2P/P2P results. No parent section says whether records and GEPA side_info strip these fields. AC-5's test checks only the worktree contents and the proposer trajectory. An implementation that hands raw rows to the reflection model and proposer passes AC-2 and AC-5 while violating invariant 2.

AC-3 says 'a second evolve run over an unchanged panel and unchanged agent CLI makes no baseline-arm model call'. AC-8 and invariant 4 require delta reports 'without re-running baseline arms'. But Approach step 1 puts the env fingerprint (child c1: toolchain versions plus lockfile hash) and the harness digest into the run key. The only refreeze path the spec defines, in AC-8 and in Risks at spec line 163, covers an agent CLI change; the child refuses to start only on a CLI version mismatch. Host toolchain drift between or during multi-day evolve runs therefore leaves no matching baseline row, for example a Go, Rust, or uv Python update while the panel and CLI stay the same. Risks line 163 concedes that 'the run key keeps drifted rows apart'. Under the c1 store rule the system then silently re-buys baselines, which contradicts AC-3 and AC-8. No parent statement says whether evolve must refuse, require --refreeze-baselines, or re-buy in that case. This is the toolchain half of the r2 baseline-drift contradiction, and it is still open.
acceptance_gaps: G-6 can be satisfied vacuously (Acceptance AC-4, Test Contracts AC-4 row). AC-4 is the only parent AC for G-6, and the spec allows labels and critiques only 'while the judge meets its calibration threshold' (Approach step 3). No parent AC requires the judge ever to produce a calibrated label set. None makes the run refuse or report when calibration fails, the way AC-1 and Risks do for G-1. The two contracted tests, test_score_ignores_labels_and_critiques and test_uncalibrated_judge_withholds_labels, exercise only the negative branches. So an implementation with no judge, or a judge.calibrate that never reaches the threshold, passes every parent test, and no label ever slices a report or reaches reflection. Nothing at the parent seam observes 'a model judge decides where structural tools apply'.

G-3 is not observed at the parent test seam (Test Contracts AC-1 row). AC-1's text requires rg_search_dispatch, rg_trait_implementors, gin_servehttp_flow, and one admitted Go and one admitted Rust SWE-bench Multilingual instance. But the expected failure of test_paid_panel_requires_every_task_family names only 'zero admitted FeatureBench tasks or no gin_edit_render_context'. An implementation of panels.load_panel that checks only the FeatureBench and Gin families passes the contracted test while starting paid runs on panels that lack the three local hard tasks or the Go and Rust instances. G-3 is the only goal no parent test fails for.
